name: AD711 / AD712 / AD713
tagline: ADI's laser-trimmed 1986 BiFET family (0.0003% THD, 20 V/µs, pA bias): the classic 1990s TL072/LF412 upgrade.

lineage.note: Sole source (AD712 ©1986–2018). 1991–92 SPICE models by ADI's PMI group. AD712-EP added later.

part_numbers.note: LF411/TL081 replacement. Mouser lists AD711JRZ; JNZ reportedly in PDN 10_0081 Rev. B.
Probably obsolete. AD711C 0.25 mV max Vos; S/T to MIL-STD-883B. TO-99 (H-8) status unknown.
PDIP-8, 0–70 °C; in Rev. I guide. Z = RoHS (lead finish, c. 2005–2006).
SOIC-8, 0–70 °C; in Rev. I ordering guide (11/2018).
Enhanced Product with own datasheet (Rev. 0); orderable number and grade unknown.
Deleted from the datasheet in Rev. F (6/2006); once 'seven performance grades'.
Four AD711-type amps on one die. JNZ reportedly in PDN 10_0081 Rev. B.

key_specs.value: 4.0 MHz typ; 3.0 MHz min (J/A/S), 3.4 MHz min (K)
0.0003% THD; crosstalk 120 dB @1 kHz, 90 dB @100 kHz
±4.5 V to ±18 V; rated ±15 V; abs. max ±18 V
25 pA (J), 20 pA (K) typ; 75 pA max; doubles/10 °C
JFET (BiFET); CM +14.5 / −11.5 V; reversal below −14.1 V

reputation.summary: A mainstream 'better' audio dual of the late 1980s and 1990s: the 1993 rec.audio FAQ lists the AD712 with NE5532, LM833, AD827 and OPA2604. Marketed as an LF411/TL081 and LF412/TL082 upgrade, it became a drop-in TL072 swap. Low THD, 120 dB crosstalk and pA bias suit high-impedance line stages and filters. Now a legacy part; no sonic descriptors collected.
typical_uses: drop-in TL072/TL082/LF412 upgrade in CD and DAC output stages
high-impedance line buffers and active filters
DAC/ADC buffers needing 1.0 µs settling to 0.01%
photodiode and electrometer preamps (pA bias, guarding)
caveats: 18 nV/√Hz is noisy next to NE5532, OP27, OPA1642 or OPA827; poor for low-impedance or MM-phono inputs.
Output phase reversal below about −14.1 V input at ±15 V; CM range only to −11.5 V.
Needs ±4.5 V minimum, not rail-to-rail; ~25 mA output is no headphone driver.
Loads above ~1500 pF need a 100 Ω isolation resistor (Figure 46).
Bias current doubles every 10 °C, raising offset errors in hot DC-coupled designs.

counterfeit_notes: None documented. The risk is fake OPA627s: ZeptoBars found an AD744 die; Head-Fi reports remarked AD711s (~18 kΩ between pins). Tell-tales: ~20 vs ~55 V/µs slew, lower supply current. Pre-Rev. D datasheets show the die photo.

silicon_changes.identification: None given. Standard lot traceability; no marking or date-code change mentioned; previous fab not named.
silicon_changes.summary: Camas, WA wafer fab qualified for ADI's bipolar process 'to ensure reliable and continuous supply'. Published 6 Jun 2025, effective 8 Sep 2025; Rev. A form and report followed. Lists multiple AD711/AD712/AD713 variants. Separate from PCN 26_0029 (Camas complementary bipolar: AD797, AD823).

spec_deltas.before: previous ADI bipolar fab (not named in the sources seen)

silicon_changes.audio_impact: None documented; ADI expects no change to fit, form, function or reliability. Typical values may shift within limits.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: same part numbers and datasheet; drop-in per ADI. Only lot provenance changes.
silicon_changes.verification: Rev. - and Rev. A forms and qualification reports found; summary confirms AD711/AD712/AD713 coverage.

refuted_claims: AD711 and AD713 do not follow the AD712 chain (Rev. I): current AD711 is Rev. E, AD713 Rev. F.
AD711 dies in fake OPA627s are not a documented decap finding (that was AD744); forum reports only, low confidence.
